To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Mg-2+ is the most effective cation for the prevention of lyses in the marine pseudomonas and that the interaction of Mg2+ with pepticoglycan contributes to the prevention of the lysis of this bacterium.

(i) the Mg-2+-dependent mechanical strength of the cell envelope of marine pseudomonads is due primarily to Mg-2+ interaction with the peptigoglycan layer and (ii) Mg-2+ ions are retained by the peptidgoglycan layer when cells are suspended in solutions containing these ions.

1) the capacity of Mg2+ salts at low concentrations to prevent lysis is due primarily to interaction of Mg2+ with peptydoylcan, 2) the outer membrane and periplasmic layers do not contribute significantly to the mechanical strength, 3) Na+ and K+, at the concentrations used, displace Mg2+ from the envelope layers, and 4) the capacity of the peptidooglycan to retain Mg2+ is related
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanism by which the peptidolycan layer of the cell walls of Gram-negative bacteria prevents the osmotic disruption of the cells when they are suspended in solutions containing low concentrations of salts.
the interaction of Mg2+ ions with the peptodoglycan layer.
the mechanism of the interaction between Mg-2+ and peptidogylcan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mg-2+-binding capacity of the peptiglycan layer of marine pseudomonads is the major determinant of the osmotic stability of the cell envelope.
Mg-2+ is the only ion that is capable of interacting with peptidolysin to prevent lysis and the interaction occurs at a concentration of Mg-2+, approximately 10-4 to 10-5 M.

the peptidolycan layer of the cell walls of marine pseudomonads, and perhaps other marine bacteria, is the primary locus of interaction of Mg-3+ and other ions in the maintenance of the integrity of the cell wall and in the prevention of lyses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Mg-2+ ions bind to peptidogylcan in the cell wall of the marine pseudomona and that the binding is a prerequisite for the prevention of lyses.

the Mg-2+, K-2+, and Na-2+ ions are not interchangeable for the prevention of lyses of intact cells and of envelope layers of marine pseudomonads, and that the peptidolycan layer plays a major role in the prevention of lyesis of these organisms.
the peptidolysin of the pseudomonad B 16, a bacteriolytic enzyme, acts by hydrolysis of the peptido-glycan layer of this organism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
magnesium is an important ion in the cell wall of the marine pseudomonal species B-16.
the interaction of Mg2+ with pepticoglycan is the main factor preventing the lysis of marine pseudomonads.
Mg-2+ is the most efficient cation in preventing the lysis of intact marine bacteria.
